title: Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes
summary: Given an undirected, connected graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, where each node i connects to all nodes in graph[i], find the shortest path that visits every node.
statement: Given an undirected, connected graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, where each node i connects to all nodes in graph[i], find the shortest path that visits every node. You can start and end at any node, revisit nodes, and reuse edges.
constraints: graph is connected, undirected, and has at most twelve vertices.
Start at any vertex and revisit vertices or edges freely.
Return the minimum number of edges in a walk visiting every vertex.
hints: A state needs the current vertex and a bitmask of visited vertices.
Start BFS simultaneously from every possible one-vertex state.
Move along edges while OR-ing the destination bit; stop at the full mask.
BFS permits revisits yet deduplicates equivalent states and first reaches full coverage with minimum edges.
editorial: BFS permits revisits yet deduplicates equivalent states and first reaches full coverage with minimum edges.

tests.explanation: Starting at one leaf and ending at another visits all four vertices in four edges.
A four-edge walk can visit all five vertices.
